## [02]{.op-number}[Compute in the]{.light} [browser]{.bold} {.op-section background-image="../images/brand/slide-section.svg" background-size="cover"}

GPU raster analytics validated against GRASS, at zero marginal cost.

## [One call,]{.light} [three rasters]{.bold}

[Watershed analysis]{.eyebrow}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
- **Accumulation, drainage, basins** from a single r.watershed run
- USGS 3DEP terrain, clipped to the drawn area of interest
- Outputs land as COG with a WGS 84 bbox and attribution

::: {.op-note}
**Note.** Threshold sets the minimum basin size in cells. Start at 10000 for a 10 m DEM.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](../blog/images/grass_watershed.png){fig-alt="Basins delineated with r.watershed"}
:::
::::

## [The same code,]{.light} [local or cloud]{.bold}

[grass.tools]{.eyebrow}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
```python
from grass.tools import Tools

tools = Tools()
tools.g_region(raster="elevation")
tools.r_watershed(
    elevation="elevation",
    threshold=10000,
    accumulation="accum",
    drainage="drain",
    basin="basins",
    nprocs=4,
)
```
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.op-card}
[Local]{.eyebrow}
Runs in your GRASS session, on your laptop.
:::

::: {.op-card .dark}
[Cloud]{.eyebrow}
Same call, submitted as a metered job. The result comes back as a COG.
:::
:::
::::
